description: One pre-scripted in-battle character talk line: who speaks, which localized text and voice to present, an optional portrait override, and the pauses around playback.

Id.technical: FName row property (declared Id, exported as ID). QueueBattleTalkSet passes each set-array ID to FindRow, and the playback state machine passes CurrentTalk->Id to OpenTalk, which resolves the row again across DTM.BattleTalkDataTables in order. The finished queue does not report this ID: it passes the owning BattleTalkSetDataTable Id to NotifyBattleTalkEnd, which fans the set ID out to every character action controller's OnBattleTalkEnd. Export keys and exported ID values match for all rows.

WaitTime.simple: Delay before the line is shown.
WaitTime.technical: float seconds; constructor default 0.0f. State 1 copies it verbatim into Timer, state 2 subtracts DeltaTime, and the line opens on the first tick with Timer <= 0.0f. There is no clamp: zero (and any negative value) therefore opens on the tick after state 1, not during queueing. Exported values range 0.0-5.0 s; 225 of 288 rows are 0.0, 50 are 1.5, and single rows use 0.5, 0.8, 1.0, 2.5 and 5.0.

Id_Character.simple: Character row whose story name is used as the speaker label.
Id_Character.technical: FName into CharacterDataTable; non-None in all 288 exported rows, with 31 distinct IDs that all resolve. Widget lookup skips None and collapses the speaker text when no row is found; otherwise it passes Character.Id_GlossaryText_StoryName to SetTextIdOnly, which resolves localized text through AGameTextManager. Separately, playback scans non-hidden managed characters (GetCharacters(false)) and uses the first whose CharacterRow.Id matches this field for the voice player slot; no match falls back to slot 0. The story-name lookup and voice-slot choice are independent.

Id_CharacterVariation.simple: Variation used to find a fallback battle-talk portrait.
Id_CharacterVariation.technical: FName into CharacterVariationDataTable; non-None in all exported rows, and all 33 distinct values resolve. It is consulted only when BattleTalkImageFileName is None: the widget follows Variation.Id_CharacterImage -> CharacterImage.BattleTalkImageFileName -> FindDynamicLoadTexture. In the export every variation in this path has a resolvable CharacterImage row with a non-None portrait name. None or any missing link leaves ImageName None and the portrait collapsed; the story phase's texture preload follows the same join with its own finders and simply adds no name on a miss.

BattleTalkImageFileName.simple: Direct portrait texture name, overriding the variation-derived portrait.
BattleTalkImageFileName.technical: FName texture-cache key, not a CharacterDataTable row ID. Non-None wins verbatim and bypasses the variation/CharacterImage join; one exported row uses T_UI_Character_BattleTalk_Image_CN_122_00. UGameWidgetManager::FindDynamicLoadTexture is only a DynamicLoadTextureMap lookup, so an unpreloaded key yields a null brush even though the widget is made visible. None selects the fallback; if the fallback also yields None the portrait is collapsed. The story phase AddUnique-collects the resolved non-None key for the current wave so it can be loaded into that cache.

TextId.simple: Localized game-text ID for the spoken line.
TextId.technical: FName passed to SerifText->SetTextIdOnly; no subtitle string is stored on this row. That setter builds a text request and AGameTextManager resolves the first matching row in its ordered current-language GameText tables (Glossary, Battle, Item, CommandList, Chat, Stamp, Story, StoryDemo, ShortStoryDemo, Tutorial, BattleSubTitle, Sound, Dlc1, Dlc2), returning empty text on a miss. All 288 exported IDs are unique and present in each of the 11 locale shards: 191 in StoryDemoTextDataTable, 68 in DlcStoryDemoTextDataTable2, 16 in TutorialTextDataTable and 13 in DlcStoryDemoTextDataTable1, with no overlap; none are in BattleSubTitleTextDataTable or BattleTextDataTable. Typing/advance is separate: the widget resets TalkVisibleCharacters, IsTalkFinished checks SerifText->IsTyping, and the queue also requires the 0.5 s hold and voice completion unless Decision is used for a bWaitForInput set.

Id_Voice.simple: Voice row ID played with the line.
Id_Voice.technical: FName into VoiceDataTable; all 288 exported IDs resolve to non-None cue-sheet/cue rows, and the alternate voice shards are not consulted by this path. PlayVoiceById rejects None, resolves the row, then PlayVoice requires a loaded cue sheet and a usable player (the requested slot if present, otherwise the first non-playing player) and returns -1 if neither is available. It uses the slot computed from Id_Character (0 when no character matches), appends _En to the cue name when bAppendEnVoiceSuffix is set and applies a VoiceVolume row override before playing. State 4 waits for typing, the 0.5 s hold and IsVoicePlaying(handle) to finish unless Decision skips those checks for bWaitForInput; it then stops the voice with a 0.0 s fade. OnEvent05 stops it only when still in state 4, OnEvent13 stops it unconditionally, and OnPrepareBattle only clears the stored handle to -1.

notes: Loaded as the single 'DataTable' primary asset BattleTalkDataTable into AGameDataTableManager.BattleTalkDataTables (+0xB40) after DTM's own DataTable loaders all report complete. Row finders walk the table array in order and take the first hit; the queue skips None TalkIds, the widget guards per-field None lookups, and PlayVoiceById rejects None.

BattleTalkSetDataTable.Id_BattleTalk supplies the talk-row IDs and their playback order. On entering a story fight, sets whose ValueType entries are all None are queued once; conditional sets are checked each tick while bBattleTalkEnabled and queued once every non-None condition passes. Tutorial state 13 queues its TalkSetIds individually with bWaitForInput=true, so Decision can end a line early.

The sequential state machine adds a fixed 0.5 s minimum after opening and a fixed 1.5 s gap after the last line; both are code constants, not fields. A line also waits for SerifText typing and voice playback to finish unless Decision is accepted.

Export cross-check: one BattleTalkDataTable asset with 288 rows, no numbered shards, and key == ID for every row. All character, variation and voice IDs resolve; all 79 set rows reference 289 talk slots, with one dangling reference (STMSN_06084M_01 -> STMSN_06084M_01_03) that the queue silently drops. One row overrides the portrait directly.

Portrait and voice assets are indirect: story-wave preload collects set cue sheets and resolved portrait texture names, FindDynamicLoadTexture reads a cache rather than loading on demand, and PlayVoice needs the cue sheet already loaded. Missing preload/data yields a null portrait brush or a -1 voice handle, not a field-level error at this table.

All mechanics here are verified in the reconstructed C++ plus the supplied exports; retail addresses are recorded in source comments. No retail Blueprint graph/asset evidence was available in the read-only inputs, and the Content export is partial, so this makes no claim about retail Blueprint overrides or about every retail row.

usages.detail: Resolves the loaded BattleTalkDataTable into DTM.BattleTalkDataTables (+0xB40).
Requests the BattleTalkDataTable primary asset during initial loading.
Story-fight enter and tick choose unconditional/conditional sets from StoryMissionWave.Id_BattleTalkSet and call QueueBattleTalkSet.
Resolves each non-None BattleTalkSet.Id_BattleTalk ID into the ordered playback queue.
Playback tick reads WaitTime, then Id/Id_Character/Id_Voice and polls typing, voice and timers.
OpenTalk re-resolves the row and renders speaker, portrait and subtitle.
SetTextIdOnly builds the request that AGameTextManager resolves across the 14 current-language text tables.
PlayVoiceById resolves Id_Voice through VoiceDataTable and the loaded cue-sheet/player caches.
FindDynamicLoadTexture reads the portrait texture cache by FName.
Story phase walks set-referenced talk rows to preload portrait texture names.
NotifyBattleTalkEnd forwards the owning set ID to all action controllers when the queue finishes.
